prompt.brief: Design a permissioned blockchain network for consortium members to deploy smart contracts, share tamper-evident transactions, integrate external systems, and govern membership and upgrades.
successSignals: Define transaction, identity, endorsement, ordering, state, and off-chain index boundaries before choosing a ledger implementation.
Use permissioned membership and an appropriate consensus protocol with explicit endorsement and finality rules.
Make contract execution deterministic, version smart contracts, and use idempotency keys at external integration boundaries.
Explain key rotation, privacy channels, node failure, governance votes, replay protection, and ledger backup.

functional: Onboard consortium members, provision nodes, deploy and upgrade contracts, submit transactions, and query committed state.
Expose transaction submission, endorsement progress, block inclusion, finality, contract events, and reconciliation status.
Support role-based identities, revocation, private data, external oracle callbacks, backups, and auditable governance decisions.
nonFunctional: Target transaction finality below 10 seconds and keep endorsement and query latency separate from block commit latency.
Scale by channel, contract, and key range while preventing one noisy member or contract from starving consensus.
Never lose a finalized block; make client retries, event consumers, and external side effects idempotent.
Degrade to read-only or queued submission when endorsement, ordering, or external integrations are unavailable.
scaleAssumptions: Operate 50 consortium nodes, 1,000 transactions per second, and multi-year ledger history.
Partition off-chain indexes by network, contract, and key; isolate hot contracts and high-volume event streams.
Retain blocks and contract versions durably while keeping query indexes, caches, and integration queues rebuildable.

metrics.label: Transaction rate
metrics.description: Drives ordering capacity, endorsement pools, state access, and backpressure.

metrics.label: Finality target
metrics.description: A transaction is business-complete only after the network's finality contract is met.

metrics.label: Durable boundary
metrics.description: Finalized blocks and contract state are authoritative; indexes and external projections are derived.

metrics.label: Async boundary
metrics.description: Keep indexing, oracle calls, notifications, and analytics off the consensus commit path.

dataFlow.title: Accept Deploy blockchain network
dataFlow.description: The Permissioned blockchain network gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The control plane records a versioned network/contract proposal and governance approvals before deployment.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Permissioned blockchain network events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume Permissioned blockchain network events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Permissioned blockchain network projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Permissioned blockchain network commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Permissioned blockchain network writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Permissioned blockchain network version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Permissioned blockchain network by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Permissioned blockchain network work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Permissioned blockchain network projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Permissioned blockchain network projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Permissioned blockchain network records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Permissioned blockchain network latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines membership, contracts, governance, consensus/finality, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and network/member/transaction keys support contracts, integrity, governance, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Permissioned blockchain network consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
